avatar.$comment: A picture beside a name (0052). The box is the shared control axis, so an avatar lines up with the field or the button it stands next to; the circle is a radius token, so a square avatar is a consumer setting one value rather than a shape input. The three fallback states share one box and one ring: the photograph is clipped by it, the initials are text against `bg`, the silhouette is the muted drawing of last resort.
avatar.$comment-size: One box, both axes, off {pct.control.height} — `req-api-size` at a component that is not a control: what the axis buys here is a row (an avatar beside a field, a comment header beside a button) sharing one height with no arithmetic anywhere.
avatar.$comment-radius: The circle, as a token rather than a `shape` input — 0050's move in reverse. `999px` clamps to half the box on a square element, so it is a circle at every size; a consumer's card style with square avatars overrides this one value.
avatar.$comment-border: The ring survives what the fill does not: over a photograph the background is invisible, over a flattened skin `surface-100` melts into the page, and in forced colours every author fill goes at once — the border is the one channel standing in all three (`req-a11y-forced-colors`).
